name: Who Stole the Lunch?
blurb: A lunch goes missing, a classmate appoints himself detective, and the clues are all there
title: Who Stole the Lunch? Mystery Comedy Skit Script for 4
description: A 5-minute mystery comedy skit script for 4: a self-appointed class detective hunts a lunch thief with fair clues and a surprise reveal. Free to perform.
h1: Who Stole the Lunch? a 5-Minute Mystery Comedy Skit Script for 4 People
logline: Rosa's lunch has vanished during maths, and Kai instantly declares himself Detective Kai. With sunglasses and a homemade magnifying glass he accuses suspect after suspect, each more ridiculous than the last. But the quiet girl peeling an orange has been watching the clues the whole time.
setting: A classroom at lunch break. Props: an empty lunch bag, a packet of crackers, an orange, sunglasses, a ruler and bottle cap as a magnifying glass, a plastic spoon, a little chocolate spread or brown face paint.

roles.name: Kai
roles.note: Student, written as a boy (any gender works). Dramatic self-appointed detective with chocolate on his chin.

roles.name: Rosa
roles.note: Student, any gender. The victim. Very hungry and losing patience fast.

roles.name: Finn
roles.note: Student, any gender. Eating crackers at the worst possible time. Suspect number one.

roles.name: Lia
roles.note: Student, written as a girl (any gender works). Quiet, observant, always peeling an orange. Solves the case.

script.scene: SCENE 1 – A classroom at lunch break

script.action: Desks pushed together. FINN eats crackers from a packet. LIA peels an orange slowly. ROSA rushes in holding an empty lunch bag upside down.

script.say: It's gone! My lunch is gone!
Gone where?
If I knew where, it wouldn't be gone, Finn! My sandwich. My orange. Gone. I left the bag on my chair before maths, and now it's empty.

script.action: KAI stands up dramatically, putting on a pair of sunglasses and holding a magnifying glass made from a ruler and a bottle cap. There is a small brown smudge on Kai's chin.

script.say: Nobody leave this room.
Kai, you have something on your chin.
A crime has been committed. And I, Detective Kai, will solve it before the bell.
Since when are you a detective?
Since thirty seconds ago. Everyone sit. Nobody eat anything.

script.action: Finn puts a cracker down, guiltily. Kai circles the desks, examining things with the magnifying glass.

script.say: Let me get the facts. One cheese sandwich. One orange. And one chocolate pudding. Stolen during maths.
Exactly. Thank you.
Suspect number one.

script.action: Kai spins and points the magnifying glass at Finn.

script.say: Finn. Crumbs on your desk. Crumbs on your jumper. Crumbs, I believe, in your hair.
These are my crackers! You can see the packet! I'm eating them right now!
A clever thief always brings his own crumbs. To confuse the detective.
That makes no sense!
Show me your hands.

script.action: Finn shows his hands. Kai sniffs them.

script.say: Cheese.
The crackers are cheese flavour! It says it on the packet!

script.action: Kai reads the packet. A long pause.

script.say: Suspect number one is free. For now.

script.action: Kai turns slowly to Lia, who keeps peeling her orange.

script.say: Suspect number two. Lia. The quiet one. Always the quiet one.
I brought this orange from home.
That's exactly what someone with a stolen orange would say.
My orange has a sticker on it. From my mum's shop.

script.action: Lia holds up the sticker. Kai examines it with the magnifying glass for far too long.

script.say: Interesting. Very interesting. Suspect number two is also free.
So who took it?
Which brings me to suspect number three.

script.action: Kai spins and points at Rosa.

script.say: Me? It's MY lunch!
Or is it? Maybe you ate it yourself in maths and forgot. Maths does that to people.
I did not eat my own lunch and forget!
Can you prove it?
I'm starving, Kai! That's my proof!

script.action: Rosa's stomach growls loudly. Kai nods, impressed.

script.say: Strong evidence.

script.action: Lia puts down her orange. She stands.

script.say: Kai. Can I ask the detective a question?
Of course. Detectives love questions.
Rosa, what did you say was in your lunch?
A sandwich and an orange.
Just those?
And a chocolate pudding. But I didn't say that. I forgot.
You didn't say it. But Kai did. "One chocolate pudding." How did you know, Detective?

script.action: Everyone looks at Kai. Kai pushes the sunglasses up.

script.say: Detective... instinct.
Second question. The pudding cup is in the bin. Licked clean. But Rosa's spoon was in her pencil case all morning. So the thief brought a spoon.

script.action: Lia points to Kai's top pocket. A plastic spoon is sticking out of it.

script.say: That's my evidence spoon. For evidence.
And third. You still have chocolate on your chin. I told you at the start.

script.action: Kai slowly wipes his chin. Looks at his finger. Silence.

script.say: Fine! It was me! I forgot my lunch, my stomach was making noises all through maths, and the pudding was looking at me! I was going to buy you a new one after school!
Then why did you make yourself the detective?
Because nobody ever suspects the detective!
Everybody suspects the detective. That's the oldest trick there is.
I'm sorry, Rosa. You can have my pocket money. And my sunglasses.
script.how: holding out the sunglasses to Rosa

script.say: I'll take the pocket money. Keep the sunglasses.

script.action: Rosa sits. Finn picks up his packet of crackers and turns it upside down. Nothing falls out.

script.say: Wait. My crackers. I had half a packet left.
Not me! I'm full of pudding!

script.action: Slowly, everyone turns to Lia. Lia calmly brushes a crumb off her sleeve.

script.say: Case closed.

script.action: Lia eats one last cracker. Blackout.

ul: Push three or four desks into a group centre stage. Finn and Lia sit facing the audience, Rosa's chair to one side, and Kai has a big circle of space to walk around them.
Put the chocolate smudge on Kai's chin before the show, small but visible to the front rows. Lia mentions it at the start so the clue is fair.
Keep the plastic spoon in Kai's top pocket from his first entrance, handle up. Nobody points at it until Lia does.
Each accusation is a spin and a point with the magnifying glass. Make the spin bigger every time, so the third one at Rosa is almost a full turn.
For the ending, everyone turns to Kai, then slowly to Lia, in two clear moves. Lia waits a beat, says the last line, then eats the cracker.
Kai has to be confident, never nervous, until the confession. A guilty detective who is having a great time is the joke.
The three accusations are the game. Each is less logical than the last: crumbs, an orange, the victim. Play every one as a brilliant deduction.
Lia barely moves in the first half. That stillness makes her stand-up moment powerful. Speak slowly and clearly when laying out the three clues.
Say the pudding line clearly the first time. The audience should be able to catch it, so the reveal feels fair, not like a trick.
Rosa's stomach growl can be a sound offstage or Rosa holding her stomach in silence. Kai's Strong evidence reply needs a straight face.
Common mistake: Kai confessing too fast. Let him try one more excuse with the evidence spoon before he breaks.
Set it in an office kitchen where a colleague's yoghurt goes missing from the shared fridge and the new intern plays detective.
With five or six people, add more suspects with their own funny alibis, for example someone who was in the toilet the whole of maths and has a witness.
Part-two hook: Lia opens her bag at the end, finds a stranger's lunch inside, and looks up at the audience. Someone else is framing her.

prompts.keyframe: A dramatic teenage boy in sunglasses holding a homemade magnifying glass over a classroom desk, two classmates eating snacks, an upset student holding an empty lunch bag, bright midday classroom light, wide shot, cinematic still, 16:9
shots: Medium shot, a teenage detective in sunglasses spins and points a homemade magnifying glass at a classmate eating crackers, comedic dramatic music mood
Close-up, slow push in on a quiet girl who stops peeling an orange and looks up with sharp eyes, the room goes still, mystery mood
Wide shot, the class slowly turns to stare at the quiet girl, who calmly brushes a crumb off her sleeve, playful twist ending

faq.q: Are the clues in Who Stole the Lunch? really fair?
faq.a: Yes. All three are shown before the reveal: Lia points out the smudge on Kai's chin at the start, Kai mentions the pudding before anyone else does, and the spoon is in his pocket from his first entrance. Sharp audiences can solve it first.

faq.q: Can we perform this at school or post it online?
faq.a: Yes. The script is free under CC BY 4.0, for school shows, competitions and videos, including monetised channels. Credit "Script: cv.cm".

faq.q: How do we rehearse the comic timing?
faq.a: Run the three accusations on their own first, with the spin and point, until they get faster and bigger each time. Then rehearse Lia's three clues slowly. The scene runs about five minutes.
